conviction_note: Event confirmed (Notice of Half Year Results, 11 Nov 2026, for 25 Nov). No sourced H1 bar exists (FY27 consensus 8.6p UFFO / 6.9p DPS only, no formal company guide, just a 9-11% TAR 'framework'). The only lean is mildly positive: peer read-across says H1 values rose (British Land +1.5% for its portfolio, Landsec an £88m surplus), and The Moor was bought at a 'significant discount' to book, which should lift NTA. Against that, operating metrics slowed in Q1 (spend +0.2%) and LTV is 44% against a 40% target, and both are already public. Findings sum +0.6; scaled number (2*0.54-1)*2.5 = +0.2. The gap is the uncertainty sitting in p_up.

Retail park capital partnership with Soilbuild/United Engineers; The Springs, Leeds bought for £73.5m (NRR 25%, £9.3m equity); proforma LTV 44% vs 40% guidance, FY27 disposal pipeline

EPRA NTA vs 105p: up, from a positive LfL valuation (peer read-across) plus The Moor revalued above its discounted purchase price
Interim at or above last year's 3.1p (which was topped up to a 94% payout); the June framework allows a higher payout
No formal guide exists. The TAR framework is likely reiterated; any comment on LTV returning to 40% or on disposals is unknown
Spend and leasing commentary for Q2 is unknown; Q1 spend slowed to +0.2%

findings.finding: Peer half-years to 30 Sep 2026 show UK retail and retail-park values still rising: British Land's portfolio valuation +1.5% (retail park leasing 6.8% above ERV, 99% occupancy), and Landsec's H1 a £88m valuation surplus. This points to a positive LfL valuation and NTA uplift for NRR, whose last three halves were +0.5% each.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NTA/valuation prints of +0.5% LfL moved the stock +0.97% (Dec 2025) and -1.17% (Jun 2026); no consistent reward
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy and is largely priced: the peers reported weeks ago, NRR is down 3.2% over 20 days and sits at about 75% of the March NTA of 105p. If the market had read across fully, NRR would have rerated with the peers. It has not, but the discount is structural, so the transmission is weak
findings.independence: Landsec H1 to Sep 2026, £88m valuation surplus against a £6m deficit a year earlier (search snippet, https://www.landsec.com/node/19556)

findings.finding: The Moor, Sheffield (90% bought for £38.3m, July 2026) was bought at a 'significant discount to the March 26 valuation' and a 10% NIY. The first valuation at 30 Sep should show a revaluation or bargain-purchase gain in NTA and IFRS profit, plus UFFO accretion against cash earning less.
findings.original_quote: The acquisition price reflects a significant discount to the March 26 valuation and a 10% net initial yield
findings.why_not_priced: The discount was disclosed but never sized. The NTA effect (perhaps 1-2p a share on ~436m shares) only appears in the interim balance sheet. It sits below UFFO and has no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction

findings.finding: The interim dividend is a new line. Last year's H1 dividend was topped up to 3.1p (94% of H1 UFFO), and the June prelims say the board has 'scope for a higher payout ratio' to smooth the finance-cost step-up, so a maintained or raised interim is more likely than a cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividend held at 3.1p in Dec 2025, stock +0.97%; FY26 DPS +3% in Jun 2026, stock -1.17%
findings.original_quote: A yield of almost 9% covered 125% at current prices is a well-protected income stream with visible upside and scope for a higher payout ratio to smooth the anticipated increasing finance costs.
findings.why_not_priced: The interim level is undisclosed. With a ~9% yield the stock trades on the dividend, and nothing in the price separates a 3.1p interim from 3.3p. Inference, sized small
findings.independence: H1 FY26 results: the interim was topped up by 0.5p to smooth Snozone seasonality (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/newriver-reit--nrr/results-for-the-six-months-ended-30-september-2025/9269027)

findings.finding: Proforma LTV rose to 44% after The Moor and The Springs, against the company's 40% guidance, which depends on an FY27 disposal pipeline. From Jan 2027 the £140m 3.5% Mall facility is refinanced by a term loan collared at 4.4-5.9%, so the interims must show disposal progress or the earnings path dips.
findings.original_quote: NewRiver's proforma LTV following this acquisition is 44%, remaining comfortably within the Company's 50% policy. NewRiver retains an active FY27 disposal pipeline of selected lower-growth assets to support a return towards its 40% guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since LTV and the refinancing terms are public. The money bought yield-accretive assets (10% and 7% NIY), not a hole, so this is signed only slightly negative and the size rests on whether disposals are named. No RNS has announced a disposal since March 2026
findings.independence: Q1 trading update gives the 4.4-5.9% collar and proforma LTV 43% (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/newriver-reit--nrr/q1-fy27-trading-update/9689887)

findings.finding: Portfolio consumer spend slowed to +0.2% in Q1 FY27 (to June 2026), from +2.3% in Q4 FY26 and +5.4% in H1 FY26, though still 200bps ahead of the Lloyds benchmark.
findings.original_quote: Consumer spending across the portfolio grew by +0.2% in Q1 (to June 2026), ahead of the Lloyds data benchmark (-1.8%), a +200bps outperformance
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: public since July. Kept at 0 because the H1 spend figure is the only part not yet seen

findings.finding: Morgan Stanley & Co. International crossed 5% three times in nine days (5.0019% on 11 Nov, below 5% on 18 Nov under the trading-book exemption, 5.0121% on 19 Nov), with no voting rights via instruments.
findings.why_not_priced: A holder oscillating around 5% under a trading-book exemption is a broker inventory or swap hedge, not a directional holder. It carries no sign, so it is sized 0

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': Q1 spend slowdown -0.1 -> 0.0 and LTV/refinancing -0.2 -> -0.1, both public since July/September
'A beat made of a one-off is sold' / one-off at a fraction: The Moor discount gain +0.3 -> +0.2, since it sits below UFFO

'Too small about the move; let reaction history move p_up, not abs_move': abs_move_pct 2.0 -> 2.5, because H1 UFFO, NTA and the dividend are new numbers, while the name's own 1.3% median kept it well below the 7% base
